label: GZ L is a positive length
statement: L > 0 and has dimension of length.

label: GZ n is a harmonic index
statement: n is interpreted as the harmonic number according to the archival transcription.

label: GZ k is natural
statement: k is a natural number according to the archival transcription.

label: Leibniz differential-rule context
statement: Treat d as the source-native differential operator for behavioral manipulation; do not impose a later limit-based foundation at this layer.

label: Tikhonov forward kernel fixed
statement: K(x,s) is fixed while testing linearity of A in z.

label: Tikhonov regularization parameter positive
statement: alpha > 0 for the smoothing functional in the source construction.

label: Tikhonov smoothing weights positive
statement: k(s) > 0 and p(s) > 0 in the source smoothing functional.

label: Lyapunov general system context
statement: X_k are functions of time and state variables; later historical transcription notes local convergent expansion for sufficiently small x_k.

label: Vlasov small-perturbation regime
statement: System (A) is written for small departures from the stationary electron-plasma state with ions treated as stationary in the initial argument.

label: Positive Vlasov density and mass
statement: N > 0 and m > 0 for the plasma-frequency behavioral tests.

label: Vlasov collisionless limiting case
statement: Set the source collision terms [∂f_i/∂t]^st to zero to inspect the collective-field transport core.

label: Chebyshev degree-n approximant
statement: U is a polynomial of degree n with adjustable coefficients.

label: Chebyshev finite approximation interval
statement: The approximation is assessed on x in [a-h,a+h], with h treated as the interval half-width.

label: Pontryagin admissible control class
statement: u(t) belongs to the fixed class D of admissible measurable bounded controls and takes values in U.

label: Pontryagin fixed control region
statement: The control region U is fixed while defining M(psi,x)=sup_{u in U} H(psi,x,u).

label: Fixed Gelfand-Levitan spectral kernel
statement: f is treated as fixed when testing linearity of the integral equation in unknown K.

label: Later Russian standard-form transcription
statement: The explicit equations are taken from a 1991 MathNet-hosted Russian source that attributes them to Gelfand-Levitan; original 1951 normalization remains a separate extraction target.
